At $95 per year, the Venture requires roughly $4,750 in annual spending to break even versus a no-fee 2% cash back card — a bar most cardholders clear in a few months. And that break-even calculation doesn't factor in the transfer partner upside, which can push the value of your miles well beyond 1 cent each, or the Global Entry credit.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first 3 months of account opening. At a minimum floor value of 1 cent per mile, that is $750 in travel — a fantastic return on a $95 annual fee card. Transfer to the right partner and you can push that well above $1,000. The $4,000 spend requirement is very reasonable for most people. As of early 2026, the welcome offer also includes a one-time $250 Capital One Travel credit valid for one year after account opening (limited-time offer — check if still available before applying).

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5x miles on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel
  • 2x miles on all other purchases

The simplicity is the feature, not a limitation. No rotating categories, no spending tiers, no activation requirements. Every dollar earns 2 miles, and those miles are transferable to airline and hotel partners — a combination that's surprisingly rare at this price point. You won't maximize every spending category, but you'll never miss a bonus either.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer to Partners: 1:1 transfers to 15+ airlines and hotels including Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles & Smiles, British Airways Avios, Avianca LifeMiles, and Wyndham Rewards. Turkish Miles & Smiles is the standout — some of the best business class award rates available anywhere.
  • Capital One Travel Portal: Book travel at 1 cent per mile. Straightforward and easy.
  • Purchase Eraser: Erase recent travel purchases at 1 cent per mile as a statement credit. Basically turns this into a 2% travel cash back card — not exciting, but reliable.
  • Gift Cards & Cash Back: Available but at reduced value — hard pass.

The optimal play is accumulating miles and transferring to partners for outsized value, particularly on premium cabin flights. For simpler needs, the Purchase Eraser is a hassle-free alternative that still returns an effective 2% back on travel purchases. Either way, you're getting solid value.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit: Up to $120 every 4 years. Every traveler should have this.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use freely when traveling internationally.
  • Travel Accident Insurance: Coverage for accidental death or dismemberment when the card is used to purchase travel.
  • Auto Rental CDW: Secondary collision damage waiver when renting a car and declining the rental company's coverage.
  • 24/7 Travel Assistance: Access to Capital One's travel assistance hotline for emergencies abroad.

Let's be honest — the Venture doesn't come with lounge access, hotel status, or annual travel credits. It's a mid-tier card and it acts like one. If those perks matter to you, the Venture X is worth the step up to $395 for the lounges, the $300 credit, and the anniversary miles. The regular Venture is for people who want great earn rates and flexibility without the premium frills.

title: Capital One SavorOne
scouts_verdict: The SavorOne is the best category rewards card you can get with fair credit — but you need to earn that title. The $39 annual fee means you have to spend enough on dining, groceries, entertainment, and streaming to justify the cost. If you're clearing $109/month on groceries alone, the 3% cash back covers the fee and everything else is gravy. No foreign transaction fees, Capital One Dining access, and rental car insurance are perks you won't find on most fair-credit cards. But let's be real: if your credit is good enough for the no-fee Savor card, get that instead. Same rewards, no fee, plus a $200 welcome bonus. The SavorOne is the stepping stone, not the destination — and it's a genuinely good one.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Capital One SavorOne is Capital One's dining-and-groceries rewards card built specifically for people with fair credit. It charges a $39 annual fee — a change from its previous $0 incarnation — but delivers the same 3% cash back on dining, groceries, entertainment, and streaming that you'd get on the no-fee Savor card designed for good-to-excellent credit. Think of it as the on-ramp to Capital One's Savor ecosystem for anyone still building their credit profile.

Capital One revived the SavorOne name in 2025, repositioning it as the fair-credit sibling to the regular Savor card. Unlike the Savor, there's no welcome bonus and the APR is higher, but the earning structure is identical. If your credit score isn't quite in the "good" range yet and you spend meaningfully on food and entertainment, this card lets you earn real rewards while you work on getting there. Spend about $109 a month on groceries alone and the 3% cash back covers the annual fee.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3% Cash Back on Dining: All restaurants, takeout, delivery, and fast food. No cap. Your DoorDash habit is now a legitimate rewards strategy.
  • 3% Cash Back at Grocery Stores: Supermarkets and grocery stores (excluding superstores like Walmart and Target). Your weekly grocery run, paying you back.
  • 3% Cash Back on Entertainment: Movie theaters, concerts, sporting events, amusement parks, and similar venues. Fun now comes with a 3% rebate.
  • 3% Cash Back on Popular Streaming Services: Netflix, Spotify, Hulu, Disney+, and other qualifying subscriptions. Your couch time is earning money.
  • 5% Cash Back on Hotels and Rental Cars: When booked through Capital One Travel. Surprisingly strong for a fair-credit card.
  • 8% Cash Back on Capital One Entertainment Purchases: Tickets bought through the Capital One Entertainment platform. If you're buying concert tickets anyway, might as well get 8% back.
  • 1% Cash Back on All Other Purchases: Unlimited, no caps on any category. The 1% base rate is the one weak spot — a flat 1.5% card beats this on non-category spending.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Rare for a fair-credit card and genuinely useful for international travel. Most cards in this credit tier charge 3%.
  • Capital One Dining Access: Exclusive reservations at award-winning restaurants and curated culinary events, plus a free OpenTable Premium subscription for hard-to-get restaurant reservations.
  • Credit-Building Tools: CreditWise credit monitoring and alerts to help you track your progress toward better credit.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs

Regular APR28.99% Variable

Cash Advance Fee$10 or 3%, whichever is greater

The $39 annual fee is a real cost, and you need to be honest about whether your spending justifies it. At 3% back on groceries, you need to spend roughly $1,300 per year ($109/month) just to break even on the fee. If your grocery and dining spending clears that bar — and if you're building credit and can't qualify for the no-fee Savor card — the math works out fine. The 28.99% APR is steep, so carrying a balance on this card is an expensive mistake. Pay in full every month or the rewards math flips against you fast.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: There is no welcome bonus on the Capital One SavorOne. That's the trade-off for a card that accepts fair credit. If you have good-to-excellent credit, look at the Capital One Savor instead — it offers a $200 cash bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, with no annual fee. The SavorOne is not the card for sign-up bonus chasers; it's the card for people who need a solid everyday earner while they build their credit score.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 8% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases
  • 5% cash back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel
  • 3% cash back on dining, groceries, entertainment, and popular streaming
  • 1% cash back on all other purchases

The earning structure is identical to the no-fee Savor card — 3% across four major everyday categories is genuinely excellent, especially for a fair-credit card. Most cards in this credit tier offer 1-2% at best. The 1% on everything else is the only weak link. Pair it with a flat-rate card like the Capital One Quicksilver for non-category spending and you've got a solid two-card setup.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Statement Credit: Redeem cash back as a credit to your account at any amount — no minimum redemption. Simple. Clean. Done.
  • Check: Request a check mailed to you. Old school but available.
  • Gift Cards: Redeem for gift cards from various retailers, though value is typically 1:1 with no bonus. No real advantage here.
  • Automatic Redemption: Set up auto-redeem when you hit a certain cash back threshold or at scheduled intervals. Set it and forget it.

Unlike the Venture cards, SavorOne rewards don't transfer to airline or hotel partners. What you earn is what you get — a clean 3% return on your bonus categories, redeemed as cash. No optimization required, no spreadsheet needed. For people building credit, that simplicity is a feature, not a bug.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• No Foreign Transaction Fees: Extremely rare for a fair-credit card. Most cards in this tier hit you with 3% on every foreign purchase — this one doesn't.
  • Extended Warranty: Extends manufacturer's warranty by up to 2 additional years on eligible purchases with warranties of 2 years or less.
  • Travel Accident Insurance: Coverage when purchasing travel fares with the card.
  • Car Rental Insurance: Secondary collision and theft coverage on rental cars (primary for international rentals), up to the cost of the vehicle for 15 days.
  • Capital One Travel Portal Access: Book through the portal for elevated 5% earn on hotels and car rentals.
  • Capital One Cafe Perk: 50% off all handcrafted beverages at any Capital One Cafe nationwide.

Let's be clear: this is not a travel card. No lounge access, no Global Entry credit, no hotel status. But for a $39 fair-credit card, the perks punch way above their weight. No FTF, rental car insurance, and extended warranty is a stronger benefits package than most no-fee cards offer — including some designed for excellent credit. The cafe discount is a nice cherry on top if you live near one.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Fair-credit cardholders who want real category rewards instead of settling for flat 1% cards while they build their score
  • Foodies on the credit-building journey who eat out regularly and want uncapped 3% back on restaurants
  • Grocery shoppers who spend enough on food ($109+/month) to offset the $39 annual fee with 3% cash back alone
  • Entertainment lovers who go to concerts, movies, and games regularly and want cash back on the experience
  • Budget travelers with fair credit who need a no-FTF card — a rare find at this credit tier
  • Capital One ecosystem fans who want access to Capital One Dining, Entertainment, and Travel perks while building toward the Savor or Venture cards

title: Citi Custom Cash
scouts_verdict: The Custom Cash is a scalpel, not a sledgehammer. Use it for one spending category per month — groceries, dining, gas, whatever your biggest expense is — and let it auto-detect your top category for an effortless 5% return. On its own, it's a solid free card. Pair it with a Strata Premier and suddenly your grocery points are transferable airline miles. That's a free card doing premium-card work.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Custom Cash is a clever little card with one party trick, and it does that trick really well. It automatically earns 5% cash back on your highest eligible spending category each billing cycle — up to $500 in spending. No activation, no choosing, no quarterly opt-in nonsense. Citi figures out where you spent the most and gives you 5% on it. After $500, you're back to 1%.

Think of it as a surgical tool, not a Swiss Army knife. Eligible 5% categories include restaurants, gas stations, grocery stores, select travel, select transit, select streaming, drugstores, home improvement stores, fitness clubs, and live entertainment. That's a wide net. The play is simple: use this card for one specific spending category each month — groceries, dining, gas, whatever — and let it auto-detect your top category. Pair it with a flat-rate card for everything else and you've got a smart two-card setup.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Automatic 5% Cash Back: Earns 5% in your top eligible spending category each billing cycle — no activation, no choosing, no hassle. It just... works. Refreshingly hands-off.
  • Wide Category List: Ten eligible 5% categories covering dining, gas, groceries, streaming, transit, travel, drugstores, home improvement, fitness, and entertainment. Odds are, your biggest monthly expense is on this list.
  • No Annual Fee: $0 per year. Free card, 5% back. Hard to complain.
  • Citi ThankYou Points Compatible: Rewards are earned as ThankYou Points. Here's the power move: if you hold a Citi Strata Premier or Strata Elite, your Custom Cash points become transferable to airline and hotel partners. That turns 5x grocery points into airline miles. Massive.
  • 0% Intro APR: 0% intro APR on balance transfers and purchases for 15 months (then variable APR applies). Useful for big purchases or consolidating debt.
  • Citi Entertainment Access: Presale tickets and preferred seating for concerts, sports, and events. A nice cherry on top.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:

One thing to watch: the 3% foreign transaction fee means this card stays home when you travel abroad. Use a no-FTF card internationally and keep the Custom Cash for domestic spending where it shines.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: Earn $200 cash back (20,000 ThankYou Points) after spending $1,500 within the first 6 months of account opening. Six months to spend $1,500 — that's $250 a month. You could hit that on groceries alone without trying. The welcome bonus isn't huge, but the barrier to entry is basically on the floor.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 5% cash back (5x ThankYou Points) on your top eligible spending category each billing cycle, on up to $500 in purchases
  • 1% cash back (1x ThankYou Points) on all other purchases

Eligible 5% categories: restaurants, gas stations, grocery stores, select travel, select transit, select streaming services, drugstores, home improvement stores, fitness clubs, and live entertainment.

The $500 per-cycle cap means this card maxes out at $25 in 5% rewards per month — $300 per year in bonus value. Not going to change your life, but for a free card that requires zero effort, that's solid. For spending beyond $500 in your top category, you'll want a complementary card picking up the slack. The automatic category detection is based on merchant category codes (MCCs), so there's no gaming it — Citi picks your top category based on actual spending.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Statement Credit: Redeem ThankYou Points at 1 cent each against your balance. Simple and clean.
  • Direct Deposit: Cash out points directly to your bank account. Same 1 cent per point, different destination.
  • Gift Cards: Redeem for retail gift cards at 1 cent per point. No bonus, no reason to choose this over cash.
  • Transfer to Partners (with qualifying card): If you also hold a Citi Strata Premier or Strata Elite, your Custom Cash ThankYou Points pool together and become transferable to airline/hotel partners at higher valuations. This is the real unlock — your 5x grocery points become airline miles worth 1.5-2+ cents each.
  • Shop with Points: Use points at checkout with select retailers (usually poor value). Skip this one.

The real power play is pairing the Custom Cash with a Strata Premier or Strata Elite. On its own, you're getting a solid 5% cash back card. Combined with a Strata card, your 5x points become transferable currency — turning your grocery spending into first-class flights. That's a no-fee card punching way above its weight class.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Citi Entertainment: Access to presale tickets and special experiences for concerts, dining, and sporting events. Not a travel perk per se, but a nice lifestyle bonus.
  • 0% Intro APR: 15 months at 0% on purchases and balance transfers — useful for large purchases or debt consolidation if you need the breathing room.
  • Worldwide Car Rental Insurance: Secondary coverage when renting a car and paying with the card.

Let's be clear: this is not a travel card. No lounges, no Global Entry, no trip insurance beyond basic car rental coverage. The Custom Cash's value is purely in its earning rates and its synergy with the Citi ThankYou ecosystem. And that's fine — not every card needs to be a travel card.

The Custom Cash wins for hands-off 5% earning in a single category — no activation, no calendar reminders. The Freedom Flex gives you higher caps ($1,500/quarter vs. $500/cycle) and plugs into Chase's ecosystem, but you have to activate rotating categories every quarter. The SavorOne trades peak rates for broader uncapped 3% categories and no FTF. The smart play? Carry all three — they complement each other perfectly.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Single-category heavy spenders who consistently spend the most in one area each month — the automatic detection rewards predictable habits
  • Citi ThankYou ecosystem members who hold a Strata Premier or Strata Elite and want a free 5x feeder card for their points pool
  • Set-it-and-forget-it types who refuse to activate rotating categories on principle (we see you)
  • Balance transfer seekers who want 0% APR on a card that also earns decent rewards
  • Multi-card strategists who want a targeted 5% card to complement a flat-rate base card — the perfect specialist in a broader lineup

title: Citi Strata Premier
scouts_verdict: The Strata Premier is the quiet overachiever of mid-tier travel cards. Four categories at 3x for $95? Neither the Sapphire Preferred nor the Venture can match that earning breadth. The $100 hotel credit nearly wipes the annual fee, The Reserve hotel perks add genuine luxury value, and the transfer partner list — headlined by Singapore KrisFlyer and Turkish Miles & Smiles — opens up premium cabin redemptions that cards twice the price can't beat. The downsides are real: secondary car rental insurance (not primary), no lounge access, no Global Entry credit, and Citi's travel portal still lags behind Chase and Amex. But pair it with a Custom Cash for 5x in a rotating category and a Double Cash for 2x on everything else, and you've got a three-card Citi setup that costs under $200 total and punches way above its weight class.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Strata Premier is one of the most underrated mid-tier travel cards on the market — and honestly, it deserves way more attention than it gets. For $95 a year, you get 3x ThankYou Points across four major spending categories: air travel, dining, groceries, and gas. That's not a typo. Four categories at 3x. The Chase Sapphire Preferred gives you two. The Capital One Venture gives you a flat 2x on everything. The Strata Premier simply covers more of your actual spending at a bonus rate.

But the real power move is what this card unlocks: Citi's ThankYou transfer partner network. We're talking Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, Virgin Atlantic, JetBlue, and over a dozen more — mostly at 1:1 ratios. And here's the kicker: holding the Strata Premier doesn't just unlock transfers for points earned on this card. It unlocks them for your Custom Cash and Double Cash points too. That's the Citi ecosystem play, and it's genuinely compelling.

The trade-off? No lounge access, no Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit (that's the Strata Elite), and the Citi Travel portal isn't as polished as Chase's. But for a $95 card that earns 3x on the stuff you actually buy every week? It punches hard.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 10x on Citi Travel Portal: Hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through cititravel.com earn a massive 10x points — one of the highest portal earning rates you'll find anywhere.
  • 3x on Air Travel & Hotels: Airline purchases and hotel bookings made directly (outside the portal) earn 3x.
  • 3x on Dining: Restaurants, bars, cafes, food delivery — it all counts at 3x.
  • 3x on Supermarkets: Grocery store runs earn 3x. Your weekly Trader Joe's haul is putting in work.
  • 3x on Gas & EV Charging: Gas stations and EV charging stations both earn 3x. Your commute earns rewards.
  • 1x on Everything Else: The base rate is nothing special — but that's what the Double Cash is for in a two-card setup.
  • Transfer Partners: 1:1 transfers to 16+ airlines and hotels including Singapore KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, JetBlue, and more.
  • $100 Annual Hotel Savings: $100 off a single hotel stay of $500+ (pre-tax) booked through Citi Travel, once per calendar year. Applied instantly at booking.
  • The Reserve Access: Book curated luxury hotels through The Reserve by Citi Travel and get daily breakfast for two, a $100 experience credit, room upgrades, and early check-in/late checkout when available.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Take it overseas without getting hit by the 3% surcharge tax.
  • Citi Entertainment: Presale tickets and preferred access to concerts, sports, dining events, and more.
  • Points Pooling: Combine ThankYou Points from your Custom Cash, Double Cash, and other Citi cards into one transferable stash.
  • $0 Liability: Zero liability on unauthorized purchases for peace of mind.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$95
Foreign Transaction FeesNone
Authorized User Fee$0

$95 is the going rate for a mid-tier travel card in 2026 — the CSP, Venture, and Strata Premier all land at the same price point. The difference is the $100 annual hotel savings benefit, which can wipe out the entire fee with a single qualifying booking through Citi Travel. Throw in The Reserve hotel perks when you stay at luxury properties, and this card can more than pay for itself before you even redeem a single point.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 60,000 bonus ThankYou Points after spending $4,000 in the first 3 months of account opening. At the floor value of 1 cent per point, that's $600 cash back. Transfer to the right airline partner — say, Turkish Miles & Smiles for a Star Alliance business class sweet spot — and you could extract $800+ in value. The $4,000 spend requirement is very doable for most households.

Eligibility note: You won't qualify if you've received a welcome bonus on a Citi Premier or Citi Strata Premier account in the past 48 months, or converted another Citi account where you earned a bonus during that same window. Citi's bonus rules are strict, so plan accordingly.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 10x points — Hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through cititravel.com
  • 3x points — Air travel and hotel purchases (booked directly, outside the portal)
  • 3x points — Restaurants and dining
  • 3x points — Supermarkets and grocery stores
  • 3x points — Gas stations and EV charging stations
  • 1x points — All other purchases

The headline here is breadth. Most $95 travel cards make you pick your poison — dining OR travel OR groceries. The Strata Premier says "all of the above" at 3x. If your household spends on groceries, eats out, fills up the car, and travels a few times a year, you're earning 3x on a massive chunk of your budget without even trying. The 10x on portal bookings is gravy — though the Citi Travel portal experience is a work in progress compared to Chase or Amex, so YMMV on whether you want to use it for hotel bookings.

No cap on points earned, and points never expire as long as the account is open. That's a quiet but meaningful perk.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Transfer to Partners (best value): 1:1 transfers to 16+ airlines and hotels — Singapore KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, Air France/KLM Flying Blue, Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, JetBlue TrueBlue, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Avianca LifeMiles, Etihad Guest, Emirates Skywards (1:0.8 ratio), EVA Air, Qantas, Qatar Airways, Thai Airways, Aeromexico, Choice Privileges, Wyndham Rewards, and Accor Live Limitless. Minimum transfer: 1,000 points in increments of 1,000.
  • Citi Travel Portal: Book flights, hotels, car rentals, and attractions at 1 cent per point. Functional but not flashy.
  • Cash Back: Statement credit, check, or direct deposit at 1 cent per point.
  • Shop with Points: Amazon, CVS, and other online retailers. Terrible value — avoid this.
  • Gift Cards: Various retailers through thankyou.com. Rarely better than 1 cpp.

The whole point of this card is transfer partners. Singapore KrisFlyer is the crown jewel — one of the best ways to book Star Alliance business and first class at a fraction of the cash price. Turkish Miles & Smiles is another standout for United-operated flights at fixed award rates. Wyndham transfers at 1:1 can be surprisingly useful for domestic hotel stays. Note that Emirates transfers at a 1:0.8 ratio (1,000 points = 800 Skywards miles), which is less favorable but still usable for Emirates redemptions.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Annual Hotel Savings: $100 off a single hotel booking of $500+ (excluding taxes and fees) through cititravel.com or by calling 1-833-737-1288, once per calendar year. You must pre-pay the full stay with your Strata Premier card, ThankYou points, or a combination. The discount applies instantly at booking.
  • The Reserve by Citi Travel: Access to a curated collection of luxury 4.5- and 5-star hotels with perks: daily breakfast for two, $100 experience credit for on-property spending (spa, dining, etc.), room upgrades when available, and early check-in/late checkout when available.
  • Trip Cancellation & Interruption: Up to $5,000 per trip and $10,000 per 12-month period for non-refundable common carrier travel expenses when your trip is canceled or cut short for a covered reason. Must be paid with the card.
  • Trip Delay Protection: Up to $500 per person per trip for meals, lodging, and essential expenses when your travel is delayed by 6+ hours. Maximum of two claims per 12-month period.
  • Lost or Damaged Luggage: Up to $3,000 per trip if your luggage is lost, stolen, or damaged during transit by the carrier. Limited to actual purchase price or replacement cost. Two claims per 12-month period.
  • Baggage Delay: Up to $100 per day for up to 5 days ($500 max) for emergency essential items (toiletries, clothing, chargers) when your bags are delayed 6+ hours.
  • MasterRental Car Insurance: Secondary coverage when you rent a car and pay with the Strata Premier. Covers the cash value of the vehicle, reasonable towing costs, and up to $500 in loss-of-use charges. You must decline the rental company's insurance to qualify. Secondary means your personal auto policy pays first.
  • Purchase Protection: Covers damage or theft of eligible purchases for up to 90 days after purchase. Up to $10,000 per incident, $50,000 per year.
  • Extended Warranty: Extends the original manufacturer's warranty by up to 2 additional years on warranties of 7 years or less. Maximum coverage of $10,000 per item.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use it internationally without the typical 3% surcharge.
  • Citi Entertainment: Presale tickets and exclusive access to concerts, sports events, dining experiences, and more.

Notable absences for a $95 card: no Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit (reserved for the $695 Strata Elite), no airport lounge access, and no streaming or dining statement credits. If you want those, look at the Amex Gold (at a much higher $325 annual fee). But the travel insurance suite here is genuinely solid — trip cancellation, trip delay, baggage coverage, purchase protection, and extended warranty all in one $95 package. Most people undervalue this stuff until they need it.

At the same $95 price point, the Strata Premier wins on earning breadth — four categories at 3x versus the CSP's two bonus categories and the Venture's flat 2x. The $100 hotel credit is double what the CSP offers. Where the CSP fights back: a more polished travel portal, the mature Chase ecosystem (Freedom Unlimited + Flex feeding into Sapphire), and arguably stronger transfer partners for domestic travel. The Venture wins on simplicity — 2x everything, no categories to think about, plus Capital One's improving partner list. The Amex Gold is a different beast entirely at $325: higher earning on dining and groceries, plus over $300 in annual statement credits that can offset most of the fee, but it costs more than 3x the Strata Premier and doesn't earn bonus rates on gas or general travel.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Families who spend broadly across groceries, gas, dining, and travel — and want 3x on all of it without juggling multiple cards or tracking rotating categories.
  • Award travel enthusiasts who want access to Singapore KrisFlyer, Turkish Miles & Smiles, and Flying Blue in their transfer partner toolkit.
  • Citi ecosystem builders pairing with a Custom Cash (5x in one category) and/or Double Cash (2x on everything) to funnel all points into one transferable pool.
  • Budget-conscious travelers who want the most everyday earning power for $95 — the Strata Premier puts more points in your pocket across common spending categories than any other card at this price.
  • International travelers who need no foreign transaction fees and a respectable travel insurance package without paying $300+ annually.

title: Citi Strata Elite
scouts_verdict: The Strata Elite is Citi's most serious premium card ever — and it legitimately competes. The earning rates through Citi Travel are best-in-class (12x on hotels is wild), the $700+ in annual credits can more than offset the $595 fee, and AA transfer access at 1:1 is a genuine differentiator no other transferable currency offers. The Admirals Club passes and Priority Pass together give you solid lounge coverage. Where it stumbles: the insurance package trails the CSR (secondary domestic car rental, no baggage delay coverage), the best earning rates require portal booking, and the 6-hour trip delay trigger is just average. If you're a Citi ecosystem person or an AA loyalist who also wants transferable points flexibility, this is your card. If you want set-it-and-forget-it simplicity, the Venture X still wins on pure value.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Strata Elite is Citi finally throwing a haymaker at the premium travel card heavyweights. Launched in July 2025 as the world's first Mastercard World Legend card, it carries a $595 annual fee and comes loaded with up to 12x earning on portal hotel bookings, a stack of annual credits worth up to $700+, Admirals Club passes, Priority Pass Select, and a solid insurance package.

This is Citi's direct shot at the Chase Sapphire Reserve and Capital One Venture X — and honestly, it's a compelling one. The earning rates through Citi Travel are aggressive, the Splurge and Blacklane credits add genuine flexibility, and access to 22 ThankYou transfer partners (including American Airlines at 1:1) gives you real firepower for premium redemptions. The card isn't perfect — the insurance benefits lag behind the CSR in a couple of areas, and some credits require booking through Citi's portal — but if you're in the Citi ecosystem or want AA access without the AAdvantage Executive card's limitations, this deserves serious consideration.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Up to 12x points per $1 on hotels, car rentals, and attractions booked through cititravel.com
  • 6x points per $1 on flights booked through cititravel.com
  • 6x points per $1 at restaurants on Citi Nights purchases (Friday & Saturday, 6 PM – 6 AM ET)
  • 3x points per $1 at restaurants and restaurant delivery services (all other times)
  • 1.5x points per $1 on everything else — no dead categories
  • $300 annual hotel credit on stays of 2+ nights through Citi Travel
  • $200 annual Splurge Credit — choose up to 2 brands from 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training, or Live Nation
  • $200 annual Blacklane credit — $100 Jan–Jun, $100 Jul–Dec for chauffeur rides
  • 4 Admirals Club passes per year for access to ~50 AA lounges
  • Priority Pass Select for primary cardholder, authorized users, and up to 2 guests each
  • The Reserve by Citi Travel — $100 experience credit, daily breakfast for two, early check-in/late checkout, room upgrades, free Wi-Fi at luxury properties
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit every 4 years
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • 22 transfer partners including American Airlines (1:1), JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines, Emirates, and more
  • Citi Entertainment — presale tickets and exclusive access to concerts, sports, dining, and arts events
  • Mastercard World Legend perks — Priceless experiences, priority restaurant reservations, 24/7 concierge, entertainment ticketing access

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual fee: $595
  • Authorized user fee: $75 per user (each AU gets their own Priority Pass Select membership with up to 2 guests)
  • Foreign transaction fees: None
  • Citigold banking credit: $145 annual statement credit toward the fee (Citigold clients)
  • Citigold Private Client credit: $595 credit in year one, then $145 annually thereafter

The math on justifying $595: you get up to $300 (hotel) + $200 (Splurge) + $200 (Blacklane) + $30/yr amortized Global Entry = roughly $730 in annual credits before you earn a single point. That's a net positive on paper — the real question is whether you'll actually use the Blacklane and Splurge credits. The Splurge Credit is flexible enough (American Airlines, Best Buy) that most people can find value, and Blacklane works for airport transfers in major cities. Citigold clients get an even sweeter deal with the fee offset.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Standard offer: Earn 75,000 ThankYou points after spending $6,000 in the first 3 months. That's worth roughly $1,200–$1,425 depending on how you redeem (portal vs. transfer partners).

A limited-time 100,000-point offer has appeared through certain channels — keep an eye out, as it pops up periodically and represents significantly better value.

Eligibility note: You won't qualify for the bonus if you've received a new account bonus on a Citi Strata Elite in the past 48 months, or if you converted another Citi card (on which you earned a bonus in the last 48 months) into the Strata Elite. Citi's 48-month rule is one of the more restrictive in the industry.

The $6,000 spend requirement in 3 months is moderate — higher than the Venture X ($4,000) but lower than some Amex Platinum targeted offers. Very doable for most people who are considering a $595 annual fee card.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
CategoryPoints per $1Details
Hotels, Car Rentals & Attractions12xMust book through cititravel.com
Flights6xMust book through cititravel.com
Restaurants (Citi Nights)6xFriday & Saturday, 6 PM – 6 AM ET only
Restaurants & Delivery3xAll other times, includes delivery services
Everything Else1.5xNo category exclusions

The earning structure here is genuinely strong. That 12x on portal hotels is the highest hotel multiplier on any major premium card — for context, the CSR gives 10x on hotels through its portal and the Amex Platinum gives 5x on flights. The 6x on portal flights is competitive too.

The Citi Nights 6x is a fun twist — essentially double restaurant earnings on Friday and Saturday evenings. If your social life runs on weekend dinners, this adds up fast. And the 1.5x floor on everything else means there are zero dead-spend categories, which is something the Amex Platinum (1x on non-bonus) can't say.

The catch: those top-tier rates require booking through Citi Travel. If you prefer booking directly with hotels for elite status benefits or airline flexibility, you're looking at 1.5x instead of 12x or 6x. That's the trade-off.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
ThankYou points transfer to 22 partners — 16 airlines and 5+ hotel programs. The headline partners:

  • Airlines (1:1): American Airlines, JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, Cathay Pacific, Emirates Skywards, Etihad Guest, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Avianca LifeMiles, Aeromexico, Thai Airways, Qantas, Flying Blue (Air France/KLM)
  • Hotels: Accor Live Limitless, Choice Privileges, Wyndham Rewards, The Leading Hotels of the World, Preferred Hotels & Resorts (I Prefer)

The American Airlines 1:1 transfer is the marquee here — Citi is the only major transferable currency with direct AA access, which is huge for domestic travelers. Singapore Airlines, Virgin Atlantic, and Turkish are also excellent for premium cabin redemptions to Europe and Asia.

You can also redeem through the Citi Travel portal, as statement credits, for gift cards, or to pay with points at checkout — though transfers to partners almost always yield the best value. Portal redemptions are decent but won't give you the outsized value of a well-planned partner transfer.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
Annual Credits

  • $300 Hotel Credit: Up to $300 off a prepaid hotel stay of 2 nights or more booked through cititravel.com. Calendar year benefit. The minimum 2-night requirement is slightly annoying but reasonable for a hotel credit.
  • $200 Splurge Credit: Pick up to 2 brands from 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training, and Live Nation. Calendar year. The AA option makes this easy to use — buy AA gift cards or pay for flights. Best Buy is also practical for everyday purchases.
  • $200 Blacklane Credit: $100 from January through June, $100 from July through December. Blacklane offers professional chauffeur services — airport transfers, city-to-city rides, hourly hires. Useful in major cities, though if you're not a Blacklane user, this credit takes effort to maximize.
  • $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck Credit: Statement credit every 4 years for your application fee.

Lounge Access

  • 4 Admirals Club passes per calendar year: Each pass admits one adult (18+) and up to 3 children under 18. Requires a same-day boarding pass for an American Airlines or oneworld partner flight. These are calendar year passes, so you get a fresh set every January. Access to ~50 Admirals Club locations.
  • Priority Pass Select: Unlimited visits for the primary cardholder and authorized users, each with up to 2 guests. Access to 1,500+ lounges worldwide (valued at $469/year for membership alone). This is the same tier offered by the CSR and Venture X.

The Reserve by Citi Travel

Book luxury hotels through The Reserve collection and get:

  • $100 experience credit per stay (spa, dining, etc.)
  • Daily breakfast for two guests
  • Complimentary Wi-Fi
  • Early check-in and late checkout (subject to availability)
  • Room upgrades (subject to availability)

These mirror what you'd get with Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts or Chase Luxury Hotel & Resort Collection — a solid perk if you're booking high-end properties anyway.

Travel Protections

  • Trip Delay Protection: Up to $500 per person per trip when your flight is delayed 6+ hours. Covers meals, lodging, and essential expenses. Round-trip travel only; must pay full fare with the card. Maximum 2 claims per 12-month period. This is secondary coverage (pays after airline reimbursement). The 6-hour trigger is standard but not best-in-class — the CSR triggers at 6 hours too, but some cards do better.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption: Up to $5,000 per trip per person, $10,000 per account per 12 months. Round-trip travel only; must pay full fare with the card.
  • Lost or Damaged Luggage: Up to $5,000 per trip ($2,000 for NY residents). Note: this covers lost or damaged baggage — the card does not include separate baggage delay insurance for purchasing essentials while waiting. The CSR does offer baggage delay coverage, so this is a gap.
  • MasterRental Coverage (Car Rental Insurance): Secondary coverage for domestic rentals, primary coverage for international rentals (outside your country of residence). Covers the cash value of the vehicle plus up to $500 in loss-of-use charges. Decline the rental company's CDW/LDW to activate. The international primary coverage is a nice touch, but the domestic secondary coverage means your personal auto insurance kicks in first for U.S. rentals — the CSR offers primary coverage everywhere.
  • Purchase Assurance Plus: Up to $10,000 per item, $50,000 annual cap. Covers theft or damage to eligible purchases within 90 days of purchase. Does not cover jewelry, watches, or gems.
  • Extended Warranty: Extends the manufacturer's warranty by up to 24 months on eligible items with an original warranty of 24 months or less. Up to $10,000 per item.

Other Perks

  • Citi Entertainment: Access to presale tickets and exclusive experiences for concerts, sporting events, dining, and arts
  • Mastercard World Legend: Priority restaurant reservations at thousands of restaurants, Priceless experiences worldwide, 24/7 concierge service, and entertainment/event ticketing access
  • No foreign transaction fees

vs. Chase Sapphire Reserve: The CSR costs $200 more at $795/year, has primary car rental insurance everywhere (the Strata Elite is only primary internationally), and includes baggage delay coverage the Strata Elite lacks. But the Strata Elite fights back with higher portal earning rates (12x vs. 10x hotels), a lower annual fee ($595 vs. $795), Admirals Club passes, AA transfer access, and a 1.5x base rate vs. 1x. If you value credits and earning, the Strata Elite wins. If you want the cleanest insurance package, the CSR still edges ahead.

vs. Amex Platinum: The Platinum costs $300 more and its credits are spread across many specific merchants (lululemon, Resy, Uber, etc.) that can feel forced. The Strata Elite's credits are more practical for most people. The Platinum wins on lounge access (Centurion Lounges are genuinely excellent) and direct hotel/airline earning at 5x without a portal. But the Strata Elite's 1.5x base rate crushes the Platinum's 1x on non-bonus spend.

vs. Capital One Venture X: The Venture X is the value king at $395 with a $300 travel credit making it effectively $95/year. It matches the Strata Elite on Priority Pass and offers Capital One's own excellent lounges. The 2x base rate on everything is technically higher than 1.5x. But the Strata Elite demolishes it on portal multipliers (12x vs. 10x hotels), annual credits ($700+ vs. $300), and the Admirals Club passes are unique. The Venture X is the budget-friendly choice; the Strata Elite is for maximizers willing to work the credits.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• American Airlines flyers who want AA lounge access plus 1:1 point transfers without being locked into an AAdvantage co-brand card
  • Portal bookers who are comfortable booking hotels and flights through Citi Travel to unlock those 12x and 6x rates
  • Weekend diners who eat out on Friday and Saturday nights and want to capitalize on the 6x Citi Nights bonus
  • Credit maximizers who will actually use the Splurge, Blacklane, and hotel credits — if you'd use all three, the card essentially pays for itself
  • Citigold/Private Client members who get annual fee credits, making the effective cost even lower
  • International travelers who benefit from no FTF, primary international car rental coverage, and a deep bench of global airline transfer partners

Skip this card if: You always book directly with hotels for elite status benefits (the portal requirement kills the best earning rates). You want primary domestic car rental insurance (get the CSR instead). You don't travel enough to use the Admirals Club passes and Blacklane credits. Or you just want a simple, low-fee premium card (the Venture X at $395 is hard to beat on pure value).

title: Citi Double Cash
scouts_verdict: The Citi Double Cash has been the default \"just give me a good card\" recommendation for years, and the ThankYou Points upgrade made it even better. Pair it with a Strata Premier and your 2% card quietly becomes a 2x transferable points card that costs you nothing to hold. If you're building a Citi setup, this is the foundation. If you just want simplicity, it's still one of the best no-fee cards around.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Citi Double Cash Card has been the answer to "what's a good simple card?" for the better part of a decade — and for good reason. It earns an effective 2% cash back on everything (1% when you buy, 1% when you pay), charges no annual fee, and doesn't ask you to think about categories, caps, or quarterly activations. It just works.

But here's the real plot twist: Citi moved the Double Cash into the ThankYou Points ecosystem, so it now earns 2x ThankYou Points per dollar instead of straight cash back. On its own, that's the same 2% value. But pair it with a Citi Strata Premier or Strata Elite and those points become transferable to airline and hotel partners — suddenly your boring grocery runs are funding business class flights. That's the kind of upgrade that turns a good card into a great one.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 2% on Everything: 1% when you swipe, 1% when you pay. No categories, no caps, no enrollment, no thinking.
  • ThankYou Points: Rewards come as 2x ThankYou Points, which become transferable to 16+ partners when you hold a Strata Premier or Elite.
  • $0 Annual Fee: Free forever. This card deserves a permanent spot in your wallet.
  • 0% Intro APR on Balance Transfers: 0% for 18 months — one of the longest intro periods you'll find.
  • Citi Entertainment: Presale access to concerts, sports, and events. Not the main draw, but a nice bonus.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$0
Foreign Transaction Fees3%
Balance Transfer Fee3% ($5 minimum) for the first 4 months, then 5%
Cash Advance Fee$10 or 5%, whichever is greater
Late Payment FeeUp to $41
Authorized User Fee$0

The 3% foreign transaction fee is the one real blemish. Leave this card at home when you travel internationally — grab your Strata Premier or any no-FTF card instead.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content: The Double Cash offers $200 cash back (20,000 ThankYou Points) after spending $1,500 within the first 6 months. Not a jaw-dropper, but the spending requirement is so low and the timeframe so generous that you'd almost have to try to miss it. It's free money with training wheels.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 2x ThankYou Points (2% cash back) on every purchase — 1x when you buy, 1x when you pay your bill

That's the whole menu. One rate, everywhere, always. No bonus categories, no spending tiers, no quarterly activation dance. The simplicity is the feature. One caveat: you need to pay at least the minimum by the due date to earn the second 1% — pay late and you forfeit the payback rewards for that cycle. So, you know, pay your bill.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Statement Credit: Redeem ThankYou Points at 1 cent each. Straightforward 2% cash back.
  • Direct Deposit: Cash out to a linked bank account.
  • Transfer to Partners (with a qualifying card): If you hold a Strata Premier or Strata Elite, your Double Cash points pool together and transfer 1:1 to 16+ airline and hotel partners — potentially worth 1.5–3+ cents per point.
  • Gift Cards: Various retailers, typically at 1 cent per point. Fine.
  • Check: A physical check (25,000 point minimum). What year is it?

The real unlock here is transfer partner access through a companion Strata card. Without one, the Double Cash is a solid 2% card and nothing more. With one, it becomes a 2x-everywhere transferable points card — think Capital One Venture vibes, but with no annual fee. That's a genuinely powerful proposition.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Citi Entertainment: Presale access and preferred seating for concerts, sports, and events.
  • 0% Intro APR on Balance Transfers: 18 months at 0%. Great for consolidating higher-interest debt.
  • Car Rental Insurance: Secondary coverage when you rent a car and decline the rental company's coverage.

Let's be honest — this isn't a travel card and it doesn't pretend to be one. No lounge access, no Global Entry credit, no trip insurance beyond basic car rental coverage. The Double Cash is a pure earning engine. Pair it with a travel-focused card and let each do what it does best.

The Freedom Unlimited earns less on the base rate (1.5%) but more on dining and drugstores, and it feeds into the Chase ecosystem. The right choice depends on which points empire you're building.

sections.title: Best For

  • Citi ThankYou ecosystem builders who hold a Strata Premier or Elite and want a no-fee 2x-everywhere feeder card

title: Bank of America Premium Rewards
scouts_verdict: Don't sleep on this one. The BofA Premium Rewards looks like a generic mid-tier card until you add Preferred Rewards into the equation. With Platinum Honors status, you're earning 2.625x on everything — a flat rate that embarrasses most premium cards at any price. Without it? Look elsewhere. This card rewards your BofA relationship and nothing else.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bank of America Premium Rewards card is kind of a sleeper. On paper, it's a $95 travel card with a decent 2x/1.5x earning structure, some travel credits, and no foreign transaction fees. Fine. Not exciting. But here's where it gets interesting: if you bank with Bank of America or Merrill and have some assets parked there, the Preferred Rewards program can supercharge this card into something genuinely elite.

With Platinum Honors status ($100K+ in qualifying balances), your earning rates jump by 75% — turning that 1.5x base into 2.625x on everything and that 2x on travel and dining into 3.5x. Suddenly this modest $95 card is out-earning premium cards that cost five times as much. The catch? You need the BofA relationship to make it sing.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 2x on travel and dining, 1.5x on everything else: Clean, simple earning structure with no caps or categories to track.
  • $100 Airline Incidental Credit: Annual statement credit for baggage fees, seat upgrades, and in-flight purchases on your chosen airline.
  • TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Up to $100 reimbursement every four years. Skip the line on BofA's dime.
  • Preferred Rewards Boost: Up to 75% more points with Platinum Honors status ($100K+ in qualifying balances). This is the card's entire personality.
  • No foreign transaction fees: Use it abroad without getting dinged.
  • Visa Signature benefits: Auto rental CDW, extended warranty, purchase protection, travel and emergency assistance.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$95

Use the $100 airline credit and you're already net positive on the $95 fee. Throw in the amortized Global Entry credit and you're making money before you earn a single point. For a mid-tier card, the fee math works out really well.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 60,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 in purchases within the first 90 days.

At the fixed 1 cent per point value, that's $600 in travel through the BofA portal. For a $95 card, that's a very strong first-year proposition. No transfer partner acrobatics needed — just book and go.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:

Preferred Rewards tiers: Gold (25% boost, $20K+ balances), Platinum (50% boost, $50K+ balances), Platinum Honors (75% boost, $100K+ balances), Diamond (75% boost, $1M+ balances across BofA, Merrill, and Private Bank accounts). Points are worth a flat 1 cent each when redeemed for travel or cash back. No guessing games, no devaluation anxiety — just clean, simple math.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Travel portal: Book flights, hotels, and car rentals at 1 cent per point through the BofA travel center.
  • Statement credit: Redeem at 1 cent per point. Cash is cash.
  • Cash back: Deposit into a BofA checking or savings account.
  • Gift cards: Available but generally worse value. Skip it.

Here's the tradeoff you make with BofA: there are no transfer partners. Zero. You can't move points to Hyatt or United or anyone else. That means no 3-cent-per-point redemptions on aspirational first class flights. But it also means no agonizing over sweet spots or watching your points get devalued overnight. You always know exactly what your points are worth. For a lot of people, that simplicity is the point.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Airline Incidental Credit: Automatically applied for incidentals (baggage fees, seat upgrades, in-flight purchases) with a qualifying airline you select each calendar year.
  • $100 TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Statement credit every 4 years when you charge the application fee to your card.
  • No foreign transaction fees: Clean for international use.
  • Visa Signature perks: Auto rental CDW, lost luggage reimbursement, trip cancellation/interruption insurance, roadside dispatch.

sections.content:

Without Preferred Rewards, this card trails the competition — the CSP and Venture offer better earning and transfer partners at the same price. But with Platinum Honors? Suddenly you're earning 2.625x on everything — no card in this price range can touch that. The BofA Premium Rewards is the ultimate "loyalty pays" card.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• BofA and Merrill customers with $50K+ in qualifying balances — the Preferred Rewards boost is the whole value proposition
  • People who want one card that just works everywhere without chasing bonus categories or managing transfer partners
  • Travelers on a budget who want a low-fee card with airline credits and Global Entry reimbursement

Let's be direct: if you don't have meaningful BofA/Merrill balances, the Chase Sapphire Preferred or Capital One Venture will serve you better. This card's superpower is rewarding banking loyalty — and nobody else in the industry does that as aggressively.

title: Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite
scouts_verdict: The Premium Rewards Elite is BofA's premium play, and for Preferred Rewards Platinum Honors members, it's quietly dominant. You get 2.625x on everything with zero category management, Priority Pass with two guests, and $480 in credits that drop the effective fee to around $70. The catch is real though: without Preferred Rewards, this is a mediocre $550 card and you should look at the Venture X instead.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite is BofA's big swing at the premium travel card segment — and whether it lands depends entirely on one question: are you a Preferred Rewards member? At $550 a year, this card goes toe-to-toe with the Chase Sapphire Reserve and Amex Platinum, but it takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of transferable points and aspirational award charts, you get fixed-value points turbocharged by Preferred Rewards, plus a pile of credits and Priority Pass for you and two guests.

For Platinum Honors members, the earning rates become absurd — 3.5x on travel and dining, 2.625x on everything else. Pair that with $300 in airline credits, a $150 lifestyle credit, lounge access, and a 20% bonus when redeeming for airfare, and you have a premium card that quietly crushes the competition for BofA loyalists. For everyone else? There are better options at this price.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Priority Pass + 2 Guests: Unlimited access to 1,400+ lounges worldwide, and you can bring two friends. That guest policy is among the most generous in the game.
  • $300 Airline Incidental Credit: Annual credit for checked bags, seat upgrades, in-flight purchases, and airline lounge fees on your selected airline.
  • $150 Lifestyle Credit: Annual credit for streaming, food delivery, fitness subscriptions, and rideshare. The kind of stuff you're already spending on.
  • TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Up to $120 reimbursement every four years.
  • Preferred Rewards Boost: Up to 75% bonus on all points with Platinum Honors status. This is where the card transforms.
  • 20% Airfare Boost: Points are worth 1.2 cents each when redeemed for flights through the BofA portal. Elite-exclusive perk.
  • No foreign transaction fees.
  • Visa Infinite: Premium-tier protections including CDW, trip cancellation/delay, and purchase protection.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
Annual Fee$550
Foreign Transaction FeeNone
Balance Transfer Fee3% (min $10)
Cash Advance Fee3% (min $10)
Late Payment FeeUp to $40

The math here is pretty compelling: $300 airline credit + $150 lifestyle credit + ~$30/year amortized Global Entry = $480 in credits. That brings the effective fee down to roughly $70 a year. At that price, you're getting Priority Pass with two guests and boosted earning rates for less than the cost of a nice dinner. Not bad.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Earn 75,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 in purchases within the first 90 days.

At 1 cent per point, that's $750 in value. Use the 20% airfare boost through the BofA portal and you're looking at $900. Combined with first-year credits, this card is heavily net-positive out of the gate — making that $550 sticker price a lot less scary.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:

Fun fact: the base earning rates are identical to the $95 non-Elite sibling. You're not paying $550 for better earn rates — you're paying for the credits, the lounge access, and the 20% airfare redemption boost. The Preferred Rewards multiplier works the same way on both cards. So if you don't need the premium perks, the regular Premium Rewards gives you the same earning power for $455 less.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
• Airfare (Elite exclusive): 1.2 cents per point for flights through the BofA travel center. That 20% boost is why this is a better flight redemption card than its sibling.
  • Other travel: 1 cent per point for hotels, rental cars, etc.
  • Statement credit: 1 cent per point. Straightforward.
  • Cash deposit: Direct deposit into your BofA checking or savings.
  • Gift cards: Available, but meh value.

No transfer partners — and that's the elephant in the room. You won't be booking Hyatt aspirational stays or United Polaris redemptions with these points. But you also won't be checking award availability at 3am or stress-refreshing for saver space. Fixed-value has its perks (pun intended). The 20% airfare bonus is BofA's way of nudging you toward flight bookings, and it's a nice sweetener.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $300 Airline Incidental Credit: Select one qualifying airline annually; covers baggage fees, seat upgrades, in-flight food/drinks, and airline lounge fees.
  • $150 Lifestyle Credit: Annual credit for eligible purchases with streaming, food delivery, fitness subscriptions, and rideshare.
  • Up to $120 TSA PreCheck / Global Entry Credit: Every 4 years.
  • Priority Pass with 2 Guests: Cardholder + 2 at 1,400+ lounges worldwide. Bring your travel partner and a friend — most cards only let you bring one.
  • Premium Hotel Benefits: Automatic room upgrades, late checkout, and complimentary daily breakfast for two at select partners.
  • Visa Infinite: Return protection, extended warranty, auto CDW, trip cancellation/interruption, emergency medical evacuation.
  • No foreign transaction fees.

sections.title: Competitor Comparison
sections.content:

Amex Platinum$695Centurion + Priority Pass + Delta + moreBroadest lounge network, most premium travel perks

The honest take: this card only makes sense if you're deep in the BofA ecosystem. Without Preferred Rewards, the CSR's transfer partners and the Venture X's lower fee are objectively better for most travelers. But for a Platinum Honors member? 2.625x on everything, no categories to track, and $480 in easy-to-use credits is a combination nobody else offers.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• BofA Preferred Rewards Platinum Honors members who want premium perks layered on top of boosted, brain-dead-simple earning rates
  • Frequent travelers who value lounge access with a generous two-guest policy and $300 in airline credits
  • Fixed-value fans who'd rather know exactly what their points are worth than hunt for transfer partner sweet spots

If you're not at Platinum or Platinum Honors tier in Preferred Rewards, save your money. The Capital One Venture X gives you a premium card experience at $395 with no banking relationship required. This card is built for the BofA faithful — and for them, it absolutely delivers.

title: Hilton Honors American Express Aspire
scouts_verdict: If Hilton is your ride-or-die hotel chain, the Aspire is still a slam dunk — even after the Priority Pass removal. A free weekend night at a Waldorf Astoria can be worth more than the entire $550 fee. Diamond status means suite upgrades and executive lounges without grinding 60 nights. And the 175,000-point welcome offer is the best this card has ever had. But be honest with yourself: if you stay at Hilton fewer than 5-6 times a year, a flexible points card will treat you better.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
If Hilton is your hotel chain — like, genuinely your go-to, not just the one you occasionally book — the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire is probably the single best hotel credit card you can get. For $550 a year, you get automatic Diamond status (the highest Hilton tier), a free night reward certificate that can be worth more than the annual fee on its own, a $400 resort credit, and earning rates that are frankly absurd at Hilton properties.

Let's talk numbers: 14x base at Hilton hotels, which stacks with Diamond status to hit 34x total. That's roughly a 17-20% return at Hilton properties. The card also earns 7x on flights, car rentals, and U.S. restaurants, and 3x on everything else. The per-point value is lower than Amex Membership Rewards (roughly 0.5 to 0.6 cents each), but the high earn rates more than compensate.

One thing to know upfront: Priority Pass lounge access was removed from this card in 2024. That stings. But Diamond status still gets you into Hilton executive lounges, and the credit package is strong enough to justify the fee for dedicated Hilton travelers. Just don't buy this card expecting airport lounge access anymore.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Automatic Diamond Status: The highest Hilton tier — normally requires 60 nights or 120,000 base points per year. You get suite upgrades (when available), executive lounge access, daily food and beverage credit, and a 100% bonus on base points. Basically, the VIP treatment without the grind.
  • 14x at Hilton (34x with Diamond): On eligible purchases at Hilton hotels and resorts worldwide. This is where the card really shines.
  • 7x on Flights, Car Rentals, U.S. Restaurants: Flights booked direct or through Amex Travel, car rentals direct, and dining out.
  • 3x on Everything Else: A respectable base rate that keeps non-category spending productive.
  • Free Night Reward: One per year (usable any day of the week), valid at most Hilton properties including Waldorf Astoria and Conrad. This alone can be worth $300-$800+ at a luxury property. Earn additional Free Night Rewards by spending $30,000 (one night) and $60,000 (a second night) on the card in a calendar year.
  • $400 Hilton Resort Credit: Up to $200 semiannually for eligible resort purchases. Spa day, dinner, golf — it all counts at qualifying resorts.
  • $200 Flight Credit: Up to $50 per quarter for flights purchased directly or through Amex Travel.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for a CLEAR+ membership.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs
sections.content:
• Annual Fee: $550
  • Authorized User Fee: No additional fee. But heads up — authorized users don't get Diamond status or lounge access.
  • Foreign Transaction Fees: None
  • APR: Variable APR on purchases (yes, this is a credit card, not a charge card — but carrying a balance on a $550 card is a choice you should not make).
  • Note: Priority Pass lounge access was removed as of January 1, 2024. RIP.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
Right now the Aspire is offering 175,000 Hilton Honors points after spending $6,000 in the first 6 months, plus a Free Night Reward. This offer runs through April 15, 2026, and it's the best welcome bonus in the card's history. If you've been on the fence, this is the time.

At 0.5 to 0.6 cents per point, the bonus alone is worth roughly $875 to $1,050 in hotel stays. Add the free night certificate — easily $300-$800+ at a Waldorf Astoria or Conrad — and your first-year value blows past $1,500 without breaking a sweat.

Pro tip: Unlike Membership Rewards cards, Hilton co-branded Amex cards have historically been exempt from the once-per-lifetime bonus restriction, though Amex has tightened rules recently. Read the offer terms carefully before applying, especially if you've held a Hilton Amex before.

sections.title: Earning Rates
sections.content:
• 14x points: Purchases at Hilton hotels and resorts (34x total with Diamond status bonus)
  • 7x points: Flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel
  • 7x points: Car rentals booked directly with select companies
  • 7x points: U.S. restaurants
  • 3x points: All other eligible purchases

Those multipliers look wild, but let's keep it real: Hilton points are worth roughly 0.5 to 0.6 cents each. So 7x on dining works out to about 3.5 to 4.2% back — good, but not dramatically better than a 4x Membership Rewards card. Where this card becomes genuinely unbeatable is at Hilton properties: 34x with Diamond status translates to roughly 17-20% back. Put every Hilton charge on this card. Every single one.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:
Hilton Honors points live in the Hilton ecosystem:

  • Hotel Stays (Best Value): Free nights range from 5,000 to 120,000+ points depending on property and dates. As a Diamond member, you may score upgrades on award stays too.
  • Points + Cash: Combine points and money for stays, though the value is usually worse than going all-points.
  • Fifth Night Free: Book 5 consecutive nights on points and night #5 is free — an automatic 20% discount on longer stays.
  • Amazon Shop With Points: Terrible value. Hard pass.
  • Transfer to Airlines: 10,000:1,000 ratio. Awful unless there's a transfer bonus and you need a small top-up.
  • Experiences and Events: Concerts, events, experiences. Value varies wildly.

The move: Redeem for premium Hilton properties — Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, LXR. A Waldorf night that costs $600+ and requires 95,000 points gives you 0.63+ cents per point. That's well above average and makes the earn rates even more compelling.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• Diamond Status: The top tier. Suite upgrades when available, executive lounge access (breakfast, evening apps, drinks), daily food and beverage credit at properties without lounges, late checkout, and 100% bonus on base Hilton points. This is the reason most people get this card.
  • Free Night Reward: Issued in year one and after each anniversary. Valid at almost all Hilton properties, including Waldorf Astoria and Conrad. Using this at a luxury property is the single best way to justify the annual fee.
  • $400 Resort Credit: Up to $200 semiannually at participating Hilton resort properties. Dining, spa, golf, resort charges — but the property must carry a "resort" designation, so check before you book.
  • $200 Flight Credit: Up to $50 per quarter for direct airline or Amex Travel flight purchases. Replaces the old $200 airline incidental fee credit.
  • $219 CLEAR+ Credit: Annual statement credit for CLEAR+ membership.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Use it internationally without surcharges.

The elephant in the room: Priority Pass Select was removed January 1, 2024. You still get lounge access at Hilton properties through Diamond status, but airport lounge access is gone unless you carry another card for that.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
The Aspire is built for one person: the dedicated Hilton loyalist who stays at Hilton properties multiple times a year and wants Diamond status without the 60-night grind. If you book Hilton resorts regularly, the $400 resort credit and free night reward can cover the annual fee before you even think about points. The current 175,000-point welcome offer (through April 15, 2026) is the best in the card's history — if this card has been on your radar, stop waiting.

Not the right card for: hotel chain hoppers, people who stay at Hilton once or twice a year, or anyone who expects airport lounge access (that ship has sailed).

title: Bilt Mastercard Blue
scouts_verdict: The Bilt Blue is the most obvious card for any renter or mortgage-payer in America. Transferable points on housing payments — for free. That alone justifies the wallet slot. The 1x everyday rate is nothing special, so pair it with a real spending card for everything else. But make sure this is the card paying your rent every single month.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bilt Mastercard Blue does one thing that no other no-annual-fee card can: it earns transferable rewards on rent and mortgage payments without charging you a transaction fee. That's it. That's the pitch. And honestly? For the millions of Americans whose largest monthly expense is housing, that pitch is enough.

Under the Bilt 2.0 revamp, the Blue earns 1x points on everyday (non-housing) purchases, with housing earnings scaling up to 1.25x based on how much everyday spending you put on the card. You also get the option to earn 4% Bilt Cash on top of your base points. And the full Bilt transfer partner network — Hyatt, American Airlines, United, Air Canada, Turkish, and more — is available at $0 per year. No other free card gives you transferable points and housing rewards. It's genuinely in a class of one.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• Earn on Rent and Mortgage: Up to 1.25x on housing payments with no transaction fees. This is the card's entire reason for existing, and it's a good one.
  • $0 Annual Fee: Free to hold. No excuses not to have it.
  • Transferable Points: Full access to Bilt's 1:1 transfer network — Hyatt, American Airlines, United, Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles&Smiles, Virgin Atlantic, and more.
  • 1x on Everyday Purchases: The base rate won't blow you away, but it's free points.
  • Optional 4% Bilt Cash: Earn 4% Bilt Cash on everyday purchases alongside your base points. Extra layer of value.
  • Rent Day (1st of each month): Special promos, bonus earning, and partner offers. It's become a whole thing.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Take it traveling.
  • Mastercard Benefits: Cell phone protection, purchase assurance, and MasterRental coverage.

sections.title: Annual Fee & Costs

Zero fees across the board. You pay nothing for the card, nothing for housing payments, and nothing for foreign transactions. The value proposition here is almost comically simple: turn your biggest monthly bill into points, for free.

sections.title: Sign-up Bonus
sections.content:
New cardholders get $100 in Bilt Cash upon approval — no spending requirement at all.

It's modest. It's not going to fund a vacation. But it's guaranteed money just for getting approved, which is more than you can say for most welcome offers. The real value of this card is the ongoing housing rewards, not the sign-up bonus.

Your housing rate depends on your Everyday Spend Ratio — basically, how much you use the card for non-housing purchases relative to your monthly housing payment:

  • 25% ratio: 0.5x on housing
  • 50% ratio: 0.75x on housing
  • 75% ratio: 1.0x on housing
  • 100% ratio: 1.25x on housing

You can also stack 4% Bilt Cash on everyday spending on top of your base points. The Bilt Cash converts at $30 per 1,000 points — a nice sweetener for everyday spend.

sections.title: Redemption Options
sections.content:

  • Rent / Mortgage: Use points to cover future housing payments — a unique Bilt perk.
  • Home Down Payment: Bilt's "Points to a Home" program lets you contribute points toward buying a home. Seriously.
  • Fitness: Redeem for SoulCycle, Rumble, and other fitness classes.
  • Dining: Redeem at Bilt Dining partner restaurants.
  • Bilt Cash: Convert to statement credits or use in the Bilt ecosystem.

Transfers are the play. Hyatt especially — you can squeeze 2+ cents per point out of premium hotel stays, which means your rent payments are quietly funding your next vacation. That's a pretty good deal for a free card.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• No Annual Credits: This is a $0 card, so no travel credits. Fair enough.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Useful when traveling abroad.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $800 per claim ($50 deductible) when you pay your phone bill with the card, up to 2 claims per 12 months. Underrated perk.
  • Purchase Assurance: Coverage for new purchases against damage or theft.
  • MasterRental Coverage: Rental car insurance through Mastercard.
  • Rent Day Perks: On the 1st of each month, Bilt runs promotions — bonus points on transfers, partner deals, sweepstakes. Mark your calendar.

Every other no-fee card earns more on everyday spending. The Double Cash gives you 2x everywhere. The CFU gives you 1.5x with bonus categories. But none of them earn a single point on your rent or mortgage. If housing is your biggest expense (and for most people, it is), the Bilt Blue fills a gap that literally no one else does.

sections.title: Best For
sections.content:
• Renters and homeowners who want to turn their biggest monthly bill into transferable points — for free
  • Points beginners who want a zero-risk entry into Hyatt, AA, United, and other transfer partners
  • Anyone who pays rent or a mortgage and isn't currently earning rewards on it (which is... almost everyone)

Don't lean on the Blue for everyday spending — that 1x rate is modest. Pair it with a stronger category card for daily purchases and use the Blue exclusively for housing payments. Think of it as a specialist, not a generalist. But as a specialist? It's unmatched.

title: Bilt Mastercard Obsidian
scouts_verdict: The Bilt Obsidian hits the sweet spot for renters and homeowners who want category bonuses with their housing rewards. At $95 with a $100 hotel credit, the fee is effectively negative — and 3x dining with Hyatt transfer access is a sneaky-powerful combo. It doesn't quite match the Sapphire Preferred's travel breadth, but no $95 card on the planet lets you earn transferable points on rent.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Bilt Mastercard Obsidian is the Goldilocks card in the Bilt 2.0 lineup — more firepower than the free Blue, less commitment than the premium Palladium. At $95 a year, it brings 3x on your choice of dining or groceries, 2x on travel, and the same housing-earning engine that makes all Bilt cards unique. Plus, the $100 annual hotel credit effectively makes the fee disappear.

Here's why it's interesting: this card plays in the same sandbox as the Chase Sapphire Preferred and Citi Strata Premier, but it brings something neither of them can — rewards on your rent or mortgage. If you're a renter who dines out a lot or a homeowner with a big grocery budget, the Obsidian gives you CSP-level category earning and points on housing. That's a combination nobody else at $95 can match.

sections.title: Key Benefits
sections.content:
• 3x on Dining or Groceries: Pick one bonus category for the year — dining (unlimited) or groceries (up to $25,000/year). Choose wisely.
  • 2x on Travel: Broad travel category earning. Flights, hotels, the works.
  • Up to 1.25x on Housing: Earn on rent, mortgage, and HOA fees with no transaction fees. The Bilt special.
  • $100 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit: Two $50 statement credits per year for hotel bookings through the Bilt portal. This wipes out the annual fee.
  • Optional 4% Bilt Cash: Earn 4% Bilt Cash on everyday purchases on top of your base points. Double dipping, basically.
  • Full Transfer Partner Access: 1:1 transfers to Hyatt, American Airlines, United, Air Canada, Turkish Airlines, and more.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees.
  • World Elite Mastercard: Cell phone protection, travel insurance, concierge services.

The $100 hotel credit more than covers the $95 fee — book one qualifying hotel night through the Bilt portal and you're net positive. Effective cost: essentially $0 or better. That makes the category bonuses and housing rewards pure upside.

sections.content:
New cardholders receive $200 in Bilt Cash upon approval — no minimum spending requirement.

No hoops, no $4,000 in 3 months. Just get approved and the $200 shows up. It's refreshingly simple. The real value, of course, is the ongoing earning on housing plus category bonuses — that's where the Obsidian pays dividends month after month.

Transfers to Hyatt are the money move. At 1.5-2.5 cents per point on premium stays, your 3x dining rate effectively becomes 4.5-7.5% back when you funnel those points into a nice hotel. That's better than almost any cash back card at any price.

sections.title: Travel Credits & Perks
sections.content:
• $100 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit: Two $50 statement credits per year for qualifying hotel bookings through the Bilt portal.
  • No Foreign Transaction Fees: Spend freely abroad.
  • Cell Phone Protection: Up to $800 per claim ($50 deductible), up to 2 claims per 12 months. Pay your phone bill with this card.
  • World Elite Mastercard: Travel insurance, rental car CDW, concierge services, and airport experiences.
  • Rent Day (1st of each month): Special promotions and bonus transfer opportunities. Set a monthly reminder.
